intended_object: Given a ring map φ : A → B between ℕ-graded rings and a homogeneous element a ∈ A of positive degree, this is the distinguished open D₊(φ(a)) ⊆ Proj B. These opens are the charts covering the domain of the rational map Proj B ⇢ Proj A that φ induces. The reading comes from the docstring and from how the opens are used in `degreeScaledDomain` and `chartCover`.
explanation:
The body is just Mathlib's `Proj.basicOpen ℬ (f a)`, that is D₊(φ(a)), with the index running over pairs (n, a) where n is a positive natural number (`PNat`) and a is in 𝒜 n. Restricting to positive degree is the right condition: these opens are exactly the ones whose union is the complement of V(φ(A₊)·B), as the next theorem in the file, `degreeScaledDomain_eq_zeroLocus_compl`, proves. That union is the natural domain of the induced map, and each chart D₊(φ(a)) is isomorphic to Spec of the degree-zero part of the localization B_{φ(a)}. This works because in the later chart maps φ(a) has positive degree (d·n with d > 0); `chartOpen` itself only needs a to have positive degree.

The setting, an arbitrary ring map between arbitrary ℕ-graded commutative rings, is the general one Mathlib uses for Proj, so nothing is too narrow. The definition is a thin indexing wrapper around `Proj.basicOpen`, built to form the open cover. It is correct as a definition of the image distinguished open.
